whatItFakes: Generated private-employer opening cash stock from real JPMC quartile/median anchors and an explicitly estimated WHO prior times scheduled payroll plus a compatible IRS nonwage accounting-cost proxy; not observed individual cash or an owner equity transaction.
why: The observed bank-account/all-debit sample differs from a generated local/territorial employer and accounting-cost proxy. Firm legal form, total size, cash-debit coverage, banking coverage, actual owner capital and individual crosswalk remain unmeasured; observed quartiles do not establish them.
replacement: Recorded firm opening balances and capital provenance, or a matched ALL-debit/balance cohort adapter with honest distributions and measured crosswalk evidence. No survival-based stock tuning or fictional contribution.

whatItFakes: A WHO-only stable per-firm startup cash-buffer rank and continuous quantile curve with one authored tail-span coefficient. Published q25/median/q75 are real observations; the full CDF and endpoints are estimates.
why: Observed cohort quartiles do not identify individual firm liquidity, uniform identity ranks, piecewise-linear interpolation, tail extrema or a coefficient uncertainty interval. Generated legal form, location, vintage and ALL-cash-debit denominator differ from the selected employer/nonemployer Chase sample.
replacement: Recorded individual firm liquidity/capital provenance or an independently observed matched ALL-cash-debit/balance cohort distribution with identified crosswalk and tail evidence. Never calibrate to future closures or wages surviving a requested year.

whatItFakes: Fresh generated public, institution, nonbusiness and unknown owners open with modeled zero-funded prototype journal cash pending genuine dated funding. The technical zero is not an observed zero balance and has no private-business calibration.
why: The superseded six-month payroll stock has no observed institutional balance, dated appropriation or funding receipt. Private JPMC employer/nonemployer cash evidence cannot supply those missing public or other unsupported owner facts.
replacement: REVIEW16 public-budget and national modules must supply genuine dated funding authority, appropriations and treasury/account receipts for represented institutions; other unsupported owners need separately source-qualified recorded funding. Preserve actual supplied balances. Never infer a measured zero, private JPMC reserve, survival stock or synthetic owner contribution.

whatItFakes: Carries a genuinely observed active 2017 county identity forward to the opening date using its official stable GID/PID alias and an already existing canonical county account. Intermediate identity-change history and actual opening active status remain unobserved.
why: The 2017 Census government listing was recorded before the January 1, 2021 opening; a later canonical directory cannot be backdated. Historical identity supplies an owner candidate, not legal powers, enacted appropriation or opening cash.
replacement: A dated opening government directory or independently sourced legal identity/change history matched to the same official government ID. Preserve the original 2017 observation date and account ID.

whatItFakes: Uses existing generated person countyIds and the observed 2020 county-to-place relation to qualify the represented share of a bounded opening purchase plan. Recorded geography and residency do not observe public demand, appropriation, custodial supplier reach, travel or delivery.
why: The county keeps its county jurisdiction while the represented cohort lives in a CDP. Census geography was observed April 1, 2020 but published August 12, 2021, so an earlier opening uses it only as a retrospective generation prior. Unverified membership remains unbound.
replacement: Dated own-county procurement/service-area records and actual contract scope with matched represented-resident coverage. A verified geographic relation alone must not close the existing public-procurement appropriation/price stopgap.

whatItFakes: P15 kin and temperament generation coefficients (relative proximity, birth spacing, first-birth spread, paternal age gap, men's fertility lag, upbringing shift, facet correlations, reference age) are prototype values.
why: Families and temperaments must be generated now; no instrument-matched source fixes these coefficients yet.
replacement: Coefficients sourced from NSFG, natality and NEO-PI-R facet tables and checked against the P15 answer keys.

whatItFakes: Kin outside the household are generated per resident household as husk-tier people: parents by the SSA 2023 life table, siblings by size-biased cohort fertility, children and grandchildren by Census children ever born; relatives are never matched to other residents, partners of siblings and adult children and cousins are absent, and residence is only county or state.
why: Every resident needs real family consistent with age; a full kin-matching and migration engine does not exist.
replacement: A kin engine that matches relatives to residents across households and places, with partners, cousins and observed migration distances.

whatItFakes: The five temperament dimensions are read from five NEO facets (CTO-approved October 10, 2026) with BLSA age curves, IPIP-NEO sex differences and NEO-PI-R manual facet correlations; the A4 compliance age curve's quadratic term is held at zero because it is not legible in the source manuscript, and each dimension uses one facet rather than its own norms.
why: The owner's five dimensions have no published norms of their own; facet norms are the nearest sourced spread.
replacement: The A4 quadratic term from a legible copy of Terracciano and others (2005) Table 2, and norms measured on the five dimensions themselves.

whatItFakes: Closeness is hours together over hours plus a sourced half-closeness point, fading by a tunable half-life; opening closeness uses the average GSS visit rate for the tie and a registered conversion of answer categories to visits, not each pair's history.
why: No survey measures closeness in hours or its decay without contact; Hall (2019) gives hour thresholds and Roberts and Dunbar (2015) only the direction of decay.
replacement: Closeness calibrated against a panel of measured tie strength and contact (for example, the Roberts and Dunbar network data or a US panel), with per-pair opening histories from the shared past.
